title: The normalized quotient root projection is invertible
statement: Use the actual completed coefficient rings, integral root line, scalar quotient line and projection-normalized IntegralRoots of [def-sfb-diagonal-coefficient-diagrams]. Let l be prime, X a scheme with l invertible in its global sections, E a finite intermediate extension of Q_l in its fixed algebraic closure, pi any integer of E, and n a nonnegative integer. Put B=O_E/(pi)^(n+1), and suppose l^(n+1)=0 in ULift B. Let roots be an IntegralRoots l E X. Let q be a B_X-linear morphism from the actual scalar quotient quotientLine to the internal free B_X-module on mu_(l^(n+1)). Suppose roots.hom followed by quotientLineMap and q equals the n-th root-tower projection followed by the free-module adjunction unit. Then q is an isomorphism. This is a statement about the actual internal module map only: it asserts no finite realization, Cartier-line comparison or ordinary realization endpoint. It needs no Noetherian, finiteness, flatness or maximal-ideal-generator hypothesis.

proof.text: The root-tower projection is locally surjective. The free-module left adjoint preserves its epimorphism. Transpose the root arrow into quotientLine by the free-module adjunction. The normalization says that its composite with q is precisely the free-module image of the root-tower projection. Therefore q is epic.

Choose the compatible primitive-root cover with its normalized finite root bases. The integral line is isomorphic to its coefficient unit there; scalar extension preserves this basis on the same slice, even for a nonflat quotient. Thus the source of q is locally free of rank one.

The integer l^(n+1) kills the quotient coefficient ring and hence the pulled-back coefficient sheaf, by additivity of inverse image. Generalize the cyclic tensor calculation of the finite root basis to that coefficient sheaf: B tensor_Z Z/l^(n+1) is B, since this integer annihilates B. Whisker the normalized root basis, then the locally bijective presheaf-to-sheaf tensor comparison. This constructs a B-linear isomorphism from the regular module to the free module on the finite roots on each of the same slices.

Restriction preserves local surjectivity, hence each restricted q is epic. Conjugate it by the two local bases to obtain an epic endomorphism of the regular module on a slice. A linear endomorphism of the regular module is multiplication by f(1). Local surjectivity supplies local preimages of 1, so f(1) is locally a unit in the commutative section rings. Cancel it and use sheaf separatedness to prove componentwise injectivity. The endomorphism is mono and epi, hence an isomorphism. Undo the bases and apply the local criterion for sheaf isomorphisms; the internal/section-module equivalence reflects isomorphisms.

proof_origin.note: The normalized projection is epic by the free-module adjunction and the locally surjective root-tower projection. Compatible root bases make its source and target rank one on the same cover. An epic regular-module endomorphism is invertible, and the sheaf local isomorphism criterion descends this conclusion.

theorem diagonalQuotientRootProjection_isIso
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (X : Scheme.{u}) (hX : IsUnit (l : Γ(X, ⊤)))
    (E : PadicAlgCl.FiniteIntermediateField l) (π : PadicAlgCl.integers l E) (n : ℕ)
    (hA : ((l ^ (n + 1) : ℕ) : ULift.{u + 1} (completedResidue l E π n)) = 0)
    (roots : IntegralRoots l E X)
    (q : quotientLine l E π n X ⟶
      (Mod.free (condensedRingObj
        (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj.{u} (completedResidue l E π n)) X)).obj
          (Scheme.proEtaleRootsOfUnitySheaf X (l ^ (n + 1))))
    (hq : roots.hom ≫ quotientLineMap l E π n X ≫ q.hom =
      limit.π (Scheme.proEtaleRootsOfUnityTower X l (Fact.out : l.Prime)) (op n) ≫
        (Mod.freeForgetAdjunction (condensedRingObj
          (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj.{u} (completedResidue l E π n)) X)).unit.app
            (Scheme.proEtaleRootsOfUnitySheaf X (l ^ (n + 1)))) : IsIso q
